content: 1. Ou Y, Bochet M, Di Martino V, Charlotte F, Azria F, Coutellier A, et al. conducted a study on the progression of liver fibrosis in patients co-infected with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV). This research was published in Hepatology in 1999, volume 30, issue 4, pages 1054–1058. 2. Di Martino V, Rufat P, Boyer N, Renard P, Degos F, Martinot-Peignoux M, et al. investigated the influence of HIV co-infection on chronic hepatitis C in individuals who use injection drugs. This long-term retrospective cohort study was published in Hepatology in 2001, volume 34, issue 6, pages 1193–1199. 3. Graham CS, Baden LR, Yu E, Mrus JM, Carnie J, Heeren T, et al. performed a meta-analysis to assess the impact of HIV infection on the progression of hepatitis C virus infection. Their findings were published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2001, volume 33, issue 4, pages 562–569. 4. Lo Re V 3rd, Kallan MJ, Tate JP, Localio AR, Lim JK, Goetz MB, et al. compared hepatic decompensation in antiretroviral-treated patients co-infected with HIV and HCV to those with HCV mono-infection. This cohort study was published in Annals of Internal Medicine in 2014, volume 160, issue 6, pages 369–379. 5. Ni JD, Xiong YZ, Wang XJ, Xiu LC. conducted a meta-analysis to determine whether an increased dose of hepatitis B vaccination elicits a better immune response in HIV-infected patients compared to the standard dose. This study was published in the International Journal of STD & AIDS in 2013, volume 24, issue 2, pages 117–122. 6. Getahun H, Gunneberg C, Sculier D, Verster A, Raviglione M. reviewed the intersection of tuberculosis and HIV in people who inject drugs, emphasizing the need for integrated tuberculosis, HIV, prison, and harm reduction services. This evidence-based review was published in Current Opinion in HIV and AIDS in 2012, volume 7, issue 4, pages 345–353. 7. Getahun H, Baddeley A, Raviglione M. discussed strategies for managing tuberculosis in individuals who use and inject illicit drugs. This article was published in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization in 2013, volume 91, issue 2, pages 154–156. 8. Padmapriyadarsini C, Chandrabose J, Victor L, Hanna LE, Arunkumar N, Swaminathan S. examined the co-infection of hepatitis B or hepatitis C in individuals with HIV and the effects of anti-tuberculosis drugs on liver function. This study was published in the Journal of Postgraduate Medicine in 2006, volume 52, issue 2, pages 92–96. 9. Liu R, Li Y, Wangen KR, Maitland E, Nicholas S, Wang J. analyzed hepatitis B vaccination behavior and willingness among migrant workers from rural China using protection motivation theory. This research was published in Human Vaccines & Immunotherapeutics in 2016, volume 12, issue 5, pages 1155–1163. 10. Guidance on HIV testing and counseling for couples, including antiretroviral therapy for treatment and prevention in serodiscordant couples, was provided as part of a public health approach. This document was accessed on February 6, 2017, via the WHO IRIS platform. 11. Patton H, Tran TT. reviewed the management of hepatitis B during pregnancy, focusing on maternal and fetal outcomes. This review was published in Nature Reviews Gastroenterology & Hepatology in 2014, volume 11, issue 7, pages 402–409. 12. Celen MK, Mert D, Ay M, Dal T, Kaya S, Yildirim N, et al. evaluated the efficacy and safety of tenofovir disoproxil fumarate during pregnancy for preventing vertical transmission of hepatitis B virus infection. This study was published in the World Journal of Gastroenterology in 2013, volume 19, issue 48, pages 9377–9382. 13. Guidance on HIV testing, counseling, and care for adolescents living with HIV, including recommendations for a public health approach, was provided for policymakers and program managers. This document was accessed on February 6, 2017, via the WHO IRIS platform.
